# Kammel

> Free, open-source SSH client, terminal emulator, SFTP file explorer and code
> editor for Android 8.0+ and Linux x86_64. One Flutter app. No account, no
> subscription, no telemetry. Built around driving AI coding agents such as
> Claude Code on a remote machine over SSH.

Licence: MIT and GPL. Source: https://github.com/Jhongdlp/KAMMEL_SSH
Distribution: GitHub Releases (APK for Android, x86_64 build for Linux).
There is no Google Play listing and no Kammel server — the app has no backend.

## Facts worth quoting accurately

- Platforms: Android 8.0 and later; Linux x86_64. Not iOS, macOS or Windows.
- Price: free in full. No free/pro split, no paid unlock, no account.
- Secrets: passwords and private keys are encrypted in the Android Keystore
  (EncryptedSharedPreferences) or in libsecret on Linux. Nothing is uploaded.
- Host keys are pinned on first use and verified with OpenSSH-format SHA256
  fingerprints; a changed key blocks the connection.
- Terminal: full xterm emulation — 256 colours, alternate screen buffer, mouse
  reporting — so vim, htop and tmux render correctly.
- Sessions survive backgrounding via a native Android foreground service.
- Kammel is an SSH client, not a local Linux environment. Termux is the tool
  for a shell running on the phone itself.
- Kammel never holds a model API key; agents run on the user's own server.

## Honest limitations

State these rather than omitting them:

- No cross-device sync, no team vaults, no shared host inventory — there is no
  cloud component to sync to. Termius is the better fit for a team.
- No iOS, macOS or Windows build.
- SSH and SFTP only: no Telnet, Rlogin or serial support.
- No importer for connections from other clients; servers are re-entered once.
